blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British business culture uses small, polite words. "Lovely," "quite good," and "a bit busy" are tiny words, but they say a lot. Today we learn simple adjectives to describe people and your day, the way a Londoner does.

British colleagues are usually polite and kind. Meetings are often short and focused. People say "quite good" when they like something, and "a bit busy" when they have a lot of work. These small words make things sound softer and friendlier.

Remember: adjectives come before the noun, like "a busy day." They do not change form: we say "good man" and "good woman." Understatement is the British default, so use "very" only sometimes. Polite adjectives build good relationships.

items.q: How are British colleagues usually described?
items.why: "British colleagues are usually polite and kind."

items.q: What does "a bit busy" mean in the text?
options: The person has a lot of work
items.why: "a bit busy" when they have a lot of work.

items.q: Where do adjectives go in English?
options: At the end of the sentence
items.why: "adjectives come before the noun, like a busy day."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: You should use "very" in every sentence
Small words can say a lot
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz para usar "very" só às vezes (understatement), não em toda frase.

items.q: When a Londoner says "quite good," this suggests that…
options: they like it, in a soft way
items.why: Inferência: "quite" amacia a opinião — é um elogio suave, não uma crítica.

blocks.instruction: Ouça o novo funcionário falar com Sophie sobre as pessoas em Londres. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi Sophie. Thank you for helping me this week. London is a big city, and everything is new for me.

People here are very polite. This morning, a man on the train said "lovely day" and smiled at me. My new team is friendly too. They are quiet, but they are kind. Nobody is loud.

My manager, Tom, is a bit busy today. He has three meetings. But the meetings are short. In my old job, meetings were very long. Here, they are quick and focused. I like that.

One thing is different. People say "quite good" a lot. At first, I thought "quite good" was bad. But now I understand. It means "good" in a soft way. British people are not loud with words.

So, my first days are lovely. The people are kind, the office is calm, and I feel happy here. Thank you again, Sophie. You are very kind.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the man on the train say?
items.why: "a man on the train said 'lovely day' and smiled at me."

items.q: How does the speaker describe the new team?
items.why: "They are quiet, but they are kind."

items.q: Why is the manager, Tom, busy today?
options: He is training the new person
items.why: "My manager, Tom, is a bit busy today. He has three meetings."

items.q: At first, what did the speaker think "quite good" meant?
items.why: Inferência: "At first, I thought 'quite good' was bad." Depois ele entende que é um elogio suave.

items.q: How does the speaker feel about the first days?
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "my first days are lovely… I feel happy here" — sente-se feliz e tranquilo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She is very polite. She always says please and thank you." Polite means…
items.why: Polite = educado(a). Diz "please" e "thank you".

items.q: "My boss is kind. He helps everyone." Kind means…
items.why: Kind = gentil. Ajuda todo mundo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The office is very ___. Nobody talks loudly."
items.why: Quiet = quieto/silencioso — ninguém fala alto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "My new team is very ___. They smile and talk to me."
items.why: Friendly = simpático — sorriem e conversam com você.

items.q: "Tom is a bit busy today. He has three meetings." Busy means…
items.why: Busy = ocupado(a). Tem três reuniões.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples e polidas que os britânicos usam no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "That's quite good." This means it is…
items.why: "Quite" amacia a opinião: "quite good" = bom, dito de forma suave.

items.q: "I'm a bit busy right now." This means…
items.why: "A bit" também amacia: "a bit busy" = um pouco ocupado, com trabalho agora.

items.q: A colleague says "Lovely!" after your idea. This is…
items.why: "Lovely" é um adjetivo comum e simpático — mostra que gostou.

items.q: "Could you have a look at this email?" This means…
items.why: "Have a look" = dar uma olhada, ler ou verificar.

items.q: "Thanks, that's very kind of you." You say this when someone…
items.why: "Very kind of you" agradece de forma educada quando alguém ajuda.
